result.title: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards
result.summary: Effective collaboration among large language model (LLM) agents in multi-agent systems requires sharing relevant evidence, requesting missing information, and incorporating teammates' contributions into decisions. Training these behaviors is challenging because final task outcomes provide limited feedback on the value of individual messages. We introduce CoSIR (Collaboration via Surprisal-based Information Rewards), a post-training approach that uses a simple, verifiable environment to teach collaboration behaviors that generalize to more complex, unseen tasks. We propose a Bayesian evaluator that scores shared information by its reduction in team surprisal, defined as the sum of the negative log probabilities assigned to the correct option given each agent's available evidence. Requests are scored by the potential reduction in the same quantity if the requested information were truthfully provided. Separate rewards encourage agents to use the received information in their private choices and calculations. We post-train Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-3-4B-it through self-play and evaluate transfer to seven unseen natural-language collaboration tasks. CoSIR achieves the highest aggregate score, while its performance in general tasks remains competitive. Behavioral analyses show increased disclosure of private evidence and fewer judged failures to use teammates' input.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CoSIR：用贝叶斯评估器以团队 surprisal 的下降衡量共享信息与请求信息的价值，作为可验证奖励，并用自博弈后训练多个 LLM，测试其向七个未见自然语言协作任务的迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「surprisal 下降即信息价值」的奖励设计以及「是否真正使用队友信息」的辅助监督，可能为 LVR 中证据 token 的贡献分配、LOOK 的证据价值评估与视觉旁路诊断提供可核查线索；但本文无视觉输入与 latent 状态，属方法借鉴而非直接竞争。
